html:
On 23 August 1966 about 200 Gurindji stockmen and their families, led by Vincent Lingiari, walked off the Wave Hill cattle station in the Northern Territory in protest at pay and conditions.

The strike turned into a claim for their land. They camped at Wattie Creek for years, and won support from unions and the public across Australia.

In 1975 Prime Minister Gough Whitlam poured a handful of soil into Lingiari's hand, handing back part of the land. The walk-off led to the Aboriginal Land Rights Act of 1976 and paved the way for Mabo and native title. Compare the 1967 referendum.
sum: On 23 August 1966 about 200 Gurindji stockmen and their families, led by Vincent Lingiari, walked off the Wave Hill cattle station in the Northern Territory in protest at pay and conditions.
